 Deion Sanders says CU Buffs RB Richard Young will start at Arizona State 
 Buffaloes hopeful RB Micah Welch will return from injury against Sun Devils

 Kansas State safety Koy Beasley, left, pulls down Colorado running back Richard Young after Young caught a pass in the first half Saturday at Folsom Field. (AP Photo/David Zalubowski) 
 By Pat Rooney | prooney@prairiemountainmedia.com | BuffZone PUBLISHED: November 3, 2026 at 1:51 PM MST | UPDATED: November 3, 2026 at 4:42 PM MST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Sustaining momentum hasn’t been a strong suit for the Colorado football team the past two seasons.
 Yet that’s the challenge at hand for the Buffaloes. And head coach Deion Sanders believes the Buffaloes are ready to put together the sort of November that can salvage CU’s season.
 CU’s fourth-year head coach hosted his weekly media session Tuesday, as the Buffs start turning the page from a 27-24 overtime win against Kansas State to set their sights on Saturday’s road date at Arizona State (5:30 p.m. MT, ESPN2).
 The victory against the Wildcats ended a five-game losing streak, while also ending a nine-game slide within the Big 12 Conference. The result injected a measure of confidence for a team that has been reeling, and the Buffs’ final four games include three of the six teams sitting at 2-3 within the conference — ASU, Cincinnati and UCF.
 The Buffs won’t find out until Saturday if the rekindled good vibes will turn into the first back-to-back conference wins in two years. But Sanders said the early Election Day returns Tuesday were encouraging.
 “I wish it would’ve been easier. But they did it,” Sanders said regarding the win against K-State. “They played good, sound football. We were penalized a bit, quite a bit, and we’ve been discussing that since game time. But these kids did it and they will never give up. I love what I see. (Tuesday) was one of our best practices I feel of the season. We changed it up a little bit and they responded well.”
 It was a less lively media session than a week earlier, with Sanders offering only a cursory update on the status of quarterback Julian Lewis, who was hospitalized last week after suffering a medical incident at practice.
 “He’s doing well,” Sanders said. “I spoke to his dad (Tuesday).”
 Instead, the focus was on another part of the backfield, as Sanders discussed the emergence of running back Richard Young during the win against Kansas State.
 A transfer from Alabama, Young carried the ball just 23 times all last season for the Crimson Tide, and he received only 16 carries while appearing in four of his first seven games with the Buffs.

 That changed in dramatic fashion against K-State, as Young collected 120 yards and a pair of touchdowns on his 24 attempts, averaging 5.0 yards per carry. The door was opened for Young in part because of an injury that sidelined Micah Welch, although Sanders said the Buffs are hopeful Welch will return this week.
 Sanders said Young would start this week at ASU, regardless of Welch’s availability, but stopped short of anointing Young as the featured back going forward. JaQuail Smith remains CU’s leading rusher with 361 yards and an average of 5.0 yards per carry, and Welch has gained 220 yards while averaging 4.9 yards per carry. Young’s big game moved him to third on the team rushing list (169 total yards, 4.2 per carry), and the Buffs also are getting solid production out of Damian Henderson II (144 yards, 4.6 per carry) and DeKalon Taylor (115 yards, 6.4 per carry).
 “Richard runs hard, works hard, prepares, study. Does not miss anything,” Sanders said. “He hasn’t had a pity party. He could’ve. And he should’ve. Because he hadn’t gotten his true opportunity. And he got it. That’s the most touches he’s ever in a college football game. He proved he’s more than worthy. And I’m happy that he didn’t erupt. He didn’t implode. He just kept working. He got what he deserved.”
